scope: Five user-supplied solid-waste-plan originals; bounded text screening and visual verification of the cited approval, agreement, table and map pages. Not a full page-by-page OCR review of every page or the whole repository.
preservation: Five full PDFs retained byte-for-byte. Repeated maps and embedded amendment copies are not counted as independent corroboration. The 347-page source is accurately titled as a compilation, with its original map-labelled filename searchable.

sources.name: Wexford Solid Waste Management Plan Amendment — State Approval April 19, 2011.pdf
sources.original: Wexford-2011-Amendment Wexford County 2009-2011 Solid Waste Management Plan Amendment.pdf
sources.description: State approval dated April 19, 2011, with modifications (PDF pp1–4), of the internally named 2009 amendment. Import tables list 22 counties with primary agreements and negotiated quantities (pp14–15); five export destinations appear on p16. The September 15, 2010 County vote was 7–2 (p46). The approval letter controls over enclosed replacement text; the sample ordinance is not an executed ordinance. Facility acreage/capacity and contamination-remediation history are planning context, not PFAS results, leachate deliveries or a construction permit.

sources.name: Wexford Solid Waste Management Plan Amendment — State Approval May 1, 2012.pdf
sources.original: Wexford-2012-Amendment  - removes the prior agreement and negotiated-volume requirements.pdf
sources.description: May 1, 2012 state approval of the internally named 2011 amendment (PDF pp1–2). The same 22 import counties move from agreement-required/negotiated-volume entries to primary/unrestricted entries, and the negotiated executed-agreement prerequisite is removed (p4). Export destinations expand from five to 22 (pp7–8), retaining receiving-county approved-plan authorization and licensed-facility conditions. This does not prove actual shipments, cancel existing contracts, waive shipping records or authorize all waste from every county.

sources.name: Lake County Solid Waste Plan Amendment — Wexford Disposal Authorization, 2016.pdf
sources.original: Lake-2016-Amendment - May 14, 2014 American Waste original letter requesting Lake County authorization to send waste to Wexford County Landfill.pdf
sources.description: August 31, 2016 signed DEQ approval (PDF p1; amended table p4), following American Waste Co-President Edward Ascione’s signed May 14, 2014 request (pp95–96). Wexford quantity cells are blank, not 100%. The November 5, 2013 Golder map (pp30, 98) depicts wells, leachate storage, secondary containment, a 20,000-gallon backup tank and dual-contained force main; it does not show an actual delivery to Cadillac. Facility capacity estimates on p97 are not Lake shipment totals. Conflicting local tally/minutes entries on pp64–65 and 85 are retained in the original, not silently reconciled.

sources.name: Missaukee Solid Waste Plan Compilation — Signed 1995 Wexford DPW Disposal Agreement.pdf
sources.original: Missaukee & Wexford County Public Works - Wexford County Landfill as disposal site.pdf
sources.description: Full 149-page plan compilation, including the executed September 19, 1995 Missaukee–Wexford Board of Public Works solid-waste agreement (PDF pp136–143). Section 2.3 requires an authorized commercial-hauler list (p140); payment-on-delivery terms, separately set tipping fees and a five-year mutually renewable term appear on p141. These are not numeric rate schedules, receipts or executed renewals. A signed October 13, 1998 letter certifies ten years of capacity at then-current volumes (p64). December 12, 2007 minutes attribute contamination/pricing remarks to a landfill representative (p5). The compilation also retains a July 30, 2009 siting-amendment approval; it is not the 2009 Cadillac leachate-treatment agreement.

sources.name: Wexford Solid Waste Management Plan Compilation — Including February 2007 CTI Facility Map.pdf
sources.original: Wexford February 2007 CTI facility map - Project No. 75010002-2.pdf
sources.description: The supplied file is a complete 347-page historical solid-waste-plan compilation, not a one-page map. PDF pp28 and 83 repeat the February 2007 CTI facility map, project 75010002.2, Drawing 1, scale 1 inch = 600 feet, depicting boundaries and landfill cells. Unlike the separate Golder 2013 map, this map does not label wells, tanks or a force main and does not establish groundwater direction. Historical facility profiles list wastewater-treatment sludge among accepted waste types (pp27, 82), not specific generators or deliveries. Repeated maps and embedded amendment copies are not independent corroboration.

boundaries: Signed 1995 Missaukee solid-waste agreement is not the outstanding signed 2009 Cadillac leachate agreement.
2011 approval modifies enclosed plan text; an enclosed sample ordinance is not enacted law.
2012 planning changes retain receiving-plan and licensed-facility conditions; no existing contract cancellation or shipment-record waiver inferred.
Lake Wexford quantity cells are blank, not 100%; its request and state approval are separate events.
Golder backup tank is 20,000 gallons; the separate CTI map has no wells/tank/force-main labels.
2007 contamination/pricing comments are attributed, not independent causation findings.
Filename Item_149.pdf matches September 8, 2009 minutes. Filename 842.pdf matches January 19, 2016 minutes, not Miscellaneous File No. 842.
